summary.text: Son of Teleon, Argonaut who drew out the feather a bird of Ares' island had shot into Oileus' shoulder; Hyginus, who calls him Eurybates, has him killed in Libya on the voyage home.

story.text: Apollonius names Eribotes son of Teleon among the crew, and on the outward voyage he drew out the feather a bird of Ares' island had shot into Oileus' shoulder and bound the wound. Hyginus calls him Eurybates and says he was slain in Libya on the return, with Canthus, by the shepherd Cephalion, whose flocks they were raiding.
